title: Tenant Observability Contract Lifecycle and Versioning Playbook
author: Marco Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the lifecycle, versioning rules, testing gates, and rollout procedures for tenant-specific observability contracts used during enterprise onboarding and post-go-live operations. It standardizes how telemetry schemas, labels, and SLO-related metrics are introduced, evolved, and deprecated for dedicated and private tenants. The aim is to reduce integration friction, preserve downstream SLO integrity, and provide clear rollback and remediation steps for customers and internal teams.

Goals
-----
- Provide a predictable, auditable change process for tenant telemetry schemas ("contract").
- Minimize customer-side parsing and dashboard breakage during schema changes.
- Ensure SLO and billing signals remain consistent across contract versions.
- Define operational runbooks for validation, rollout, and rollback.

Scope
-----
Includes: ingress metrics, request/response metadata, model-identifiers, latency/billing tokens, event tracing IDs, and tenant-specific labels emitted by ingress-proxy, model-router, and telemetry-gatekeeper.
Excludes: internal-only debug traces and ephemeral dev-only flags.

Principles
----------
1) Backward compatibility first: additive fields only for patch/minor updates whenever possible.
2) Explicit version header: every telemetry payload must include `telemetry_contract_version` and `schema_version`.
3) Consumer-driven validation: create a consumer schema test harness prior to rollout.
4) SLO continuity: any change that impacts token counting or latency buckets requires SLO owner sign-off.

Contract Versioning Rules
-------------------------
- Versioning scheme: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (SemVer-like, but focused on consumer compatibility):
  - MAJOR: incompatible changes (removal/rename of required fields, semantic changes to metric meaning). Requires coordinated migration and 90-day deprecation notice.
  - MINOR: additive fields and new optional labels. Safe for rolling updates.
  - PATCH: bug fixes in serialization, typos, or clarifications that do not change semantics.
- Filesystem path / registry: contracts are stored in the telemetry registry (internal git repo: infra/telemetry/contracts/). Each version has a manifest and migration notes.

Telemetry Contract Example (minimal JSON payload example)
--------------------------------------------------------
Note: this example is intentionally concise — real payloads will include additional tracing and debug metadata.

{
  "telemetry_contract_version": "1.2.0",
  "tenant_id": "enterprise-42",
  "request_id": "r-8ab3cd",
  "model_id": "redwood-compat-13b-q4",
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "tokens_input": 128,
  "tokens_output": 42,
  "latency_ms": 78.2,
  "cost_units": 0.0038,
  "timestamp": "2026-01-29T15:22:03Z",
  "labels": {"region":"eu-west-1", "deployment_tier":"dedicated", "privacy_level":"high"}
}

Migration and Rollout Procedure
-------------------------------
1) Design phase (owner: CS integration engineer)
   - Author the new contract in the registry and add migration notes.
   - Identify all internal consumers (billing, SLO dashboards, QBR reports, cost attribution jobs, alerting rules).
   - Create a migration ticket and assign reviewers (SRE, Billing, Observability, Product).

2) Validation harness (owner: Observability team)
   - Add the new schema to the consumer test harness.
   - Run the following checks:
     a) Parsing test (clickhouse/bq ingestion): ingest 1000 synthetic payloads and confirm no schema rejections.
     b) SLO equivalence: simulate token counts and latency buckets to ensure SLOs do not change >1%.
     c) Dashboard smoke: run dashboard snapshots of top-10 queries for differences.

3) Canary (owner: CS + SRE)
   - Canary window (default 48 hours): enable new contract for 2% of tenant traffic per region.
   - Monitor: error rate, ingestion rejects, billing delta, and SLO drift. Alerts: any of the following triggers immediate rollback:
     - ingestion_reject_rate > 0.1% sustained over 30m
     - billing_signal_delta > 5% compared to baseline
     - SLO metric drift > 2%

4) Gradual rollout
   - 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over successive windows (24–72 hours each), adjust based on risk and test results.

5) Complete and document
   - Mark registry entry as active and update related onboarding docs and QBR templates.
   - Notify customer success contacts and tenant POCs.

Rollback and Emergency Remediation
----------------------------------
- Hot rollback: flip ingestion to last-stable schema at the telemetry-gatekeeper layer. This is expected to be near-instant but requires a follow-up migration postmortem.
- If hot rollback is not possible (e.g., semantic change in token counting), escalate immediately to SRE and Billing and open a severity-1 incident with the standard incident comms template.
- Triage checklist for rollback incident:
  1) Capture affected tenant list and time window.
  2) Freeze billing-related aggregations and mark as provisional.
  3) Notify customer POCs with a templated message (see Appendix A).

Validation Tests and Gating
--------------------------
Mandatory gating checks before any minor or major update: 
- Schema lint (jsonschema) passes.
- Consumer test harness run with zero parsing failures.
- SLO smoke equivalence within guardrails (default: SLO drift < 1% for latency; token count variance < 0.5%).
- Billing delta within tolerance (default: < 2% over the canary window).

Sample Prometheus Alert Rule (conceptual)
----------------------------------------
# name: Telemetry_Ingestion_Rejects
expr: rate(telemetry_ingestion_rejects_total[5m]) / rate(telemetry_ingest_total[5m]) > 0.001
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "High telemetry ingestion reject rate (>0.1%)"
  runbook: "/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/telemetry-ingest-failure"

SLO Mapping and QBR Implications
--------------------------------
- Each telemetry contract version must include a metadata file that maps emitted fields to product SLOs and QBR KPIs. Example mapping: `tokens_output` -> billing.units, `latency_ms` -> platform.latency.slo.
- During QBR prep, the CS team must verify that the contract version used in the QBR timeframe matches the contract recorded in the migration registry. Discrepancies must be annotated in the QBR appendix.

Ownership and Notifications
---------------------------
- Contract author: CS integration engineering (primary).
- Observability: owns consumer test harness and alerting.
- Billing: approves any change that affects token counting or cost_units.
- SRE: approves rollout windows and manages canary routing.

Communication and Customer-Facing Steps
--------------------------------------
1) Pre-schedule notification: send a 14-day heads-up for major changes, 7 days for minor changes.
2) Pre-cutover checklist: share a migration plan and sample payloads with tenant POC and solutions engineer.
3) Post-cutover confirmation: within 24 hours confirm telemetry ingestion is stable and provide a simple validation script tenant can run.

Appendix A — Templated Customer Notification (short)
---------------------------------------------------
Subject: Upcoming Telemetry Schema Update (telemetry_contract_version 1.2.0)

Hello <Tenant POC>,

We are planning a telemetry schema update that will be enabled for your tenant on <date>. The change is additive (new optional labels and an additional `cost_units` field) and should not require action. During the canary window, you may see a small variance in billing aggregates; we will monitor closely and share results. If you prefer a scheduled cutover or need a private testing window, reply to this thread and we will coordinate.

Regards,
Redwood Customer Success

Appendix B — Example Validation CLI (tenant-facing)
----------------------------------------------------
# curl example payload to the telemetry gatekeeper (test endpoint)
curl -X POST "https://telemetry-test.redwood.com/ingest" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"telemetry_contract_version":"1.2.0","tenant_id":"<your-tenant>","request_id":"r-test","model_id":"m-test","tokens_input":10,"tokens_output":5,"latency_ms":40.0,"timestamp":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}'

# quick parse check (jq required)
cat sample-payload.json | jq '.telemetry_contract_version == "1.2.0" and .tokens_output > 0'

Appendix C — Quick Checklist (for rollout ticket)
-------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Registry entry created and reviewed
- [ ] Consumer harness run and green
- [ ] Billing sign-off obtained (if required)
- [ ] Canary window scheduled (2% start)
- [ ] Pager/alert rules adjusted and runbook linked
- [ ] Customer POC notified per pre-schedule
- [ ] Post-cutover validation completed

Related pages and artifacts
--------------------------
- telemetry contracts repo: infra/telemetry/contracts/ (internal git)
- Observability test harness: /confluence/eng-platform/telemetry-test-harness
- Incident runbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/telemetry-ingest-failures

Questions or feedback
--------------------
If you are the owner of an internal consumer (dashboards, billing jobs, or QBR reports), please review the contract registry entry during the design phase and add yourself as a reviewer. For urgent issues during a rollout, page #observability on Slack and follow the incident escalation procedure.
